subject: Staged IO maintenance window — north-us affinity & fallback guidance
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acme-analytics.com>, OpsPrime Support <support@opsprime.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staged IO maintenance window — north-us affinity & fallback guidance

Hi Samantha (and OpsPrime team),

Quick heads up: we have a scheduled maintenance window for the north-us region on Sunday, Nov 22, 2026, starting 01:00 UTC (the local curfew window). The operation is a staged IO/firmware sanitation pass on a subset of SSD controllers combined with a minor driver variant swap on a small control plane path. This is a conservative change to reduce rare tail errors we saw in our telemetry.

What we will do (high level):
- Drain a small percentage (~6%) of inference-serving nodes in staggered waves (6-minute drains per node).
- Apply firmware sanitization to IO pools, then reattach.
- For affected nodes only, switch to a previously-validated driver variant if kernel/driver mismatch is detected; automated rollback path is in place.
- Maintain KV cache preservation for warm prefixes where possible; for impacted sessions we will preserve token state via prefix checkpointing to minimize model context loss.

Expected customer impact: largely transparent for most customers. You may see brief latency spikes (200–700 ms) or occasional 503s for in-flight requests while sessions warm back up. No data will be deleted. We will not evict active dedicated capacity (Dedicated customers will see no node swaps without prior notice).

Customer guidance (if you want to avoid any risk):
- Pin to a compatible model variant for the maintenance window (add ?variant=stable-202611 in calls) — this will opt you into the fallback that avoids the driver path we touch.
- If you need a zero-interruption canary, request a reserved canary pool — we can provision for Acme (see canary link below).
- Ensure retry/backoff on 5xx responses (we will return Retry-After when appropriate).

Schedule (UTC):
- Nov 22 01:00 — maintenance starts (wave 1)
- Nov 22 01:00–05:00 — staggered waves across north-us AZs
- Nov 22 05:00 — anticipated end (we may finish earlier)

Attachments: operations checklist and the north-us node affinity map.

If you want us to hold your traffic to a canary pool, reply with the accounts/keys and intended RPS and we'll provision.

Thanks — will post updates in the thread during the window.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acme-analytics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staged IO maintenance window — north-us affinity & fallback guidance

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the early notice. Two quick asks from Acme: 1) Can you reserve a small canary pool (approx 4 GPUs) for us starting 01:00–03:00 UTC so we can validate our production traffic? 2) If you switch to the fallback driver, will embeddings be bit-identical vs current variant (we use embeddings heavily for nearline searches)?

We can accept small transient latency, but would prefer to avoid any 5xxs during our busiest batch windows (02:30–03:00 UTC). Please put the canary details in a calendar invite if you can.

— Samantha
Samantha Liu
SRE Lead, Acme Analytics
samantha.liu@acme-analytics.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staged IO maintenance window — north-us affinity & fallback guidance

Samantha — we can provision the 4-GPU canary pool. Action items for Acme: reply with the API keys/service IDs you want routed; we'll create the pool and provide an endpoint alias you can point to.

On driver/embedding parity: the fallback driver variant is byte-compatible for model weights/embeddings for all supported quantizations we serve; however, there is a documented micro-difference in tokenization whitespace behavior for one legacy tokenizer (only affects a tiny fraction of embed calls). We'll run a quick comparison during the canary window on your sample dataset if you send one (or we can run on a synthetic subset).

Rollout notes (ops):
- Canary wave at 01:00 UTC (4 GPUs reserved for Acme)
- If canary passes (no >1% error delta and <150ms p95 latency regression after 15 minutes), increment waves per standard cadence.
- Automated rollback triggers: healthcheck failure > 2 consecutive waves, or error-rate spike > 3x baseline.

I'll create the calendar invite and the temporary endpoint alias by EOD.

Marcus Lin
SRE Manager, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acme-analytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staged IO maintenance window — north-us affinity & fallback guidance

Thanks all — short update for the thread: 
- Canary pool provisioned for Acme (endpoint alias: https://canary.north-us.redwood.com/acme). Calendar invite sent.
- Ops checklist and affinity CSV attached to this thread.
- We'll post a brief postmortem with regression metrics and any driver-delta notes to the Drive link after the window; if action items come out of that, I'll loop in your CS rep.

If anything else comes up before Sunday, ping me directly. Otherwise we'll use this thread for live updates during the window.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

- 20261121-maintenance-ops-checklist.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)
